title: Practice 1: Rain falls, time flies, luck comes: the idioms

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Дождь ___ (идти — to go, walk, one way) три дня подряд.
exercises.why: **шёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **идти** (to go) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ходить** for many directions. past: он шёл · она шла́ · оно шло́ · они шли́. — Wiktionary, «идти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **идти**: to go; to walk; (of precipitation) to fall; to function, to work (of clocks and watches).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — Идёт не дождь, а снег. — It's snowing, not raining. · Часы идут. — The clock is ticking. · Идёт фильм. — A film is on. · Это платье тебе идёт. — That dress suits you. · Правительство идёт к демократии. — The government is moving towards democracy.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note the following expressions: Идёт дождь. Фильм идёт. Разговор идёт. Идёт снег. Урок идёт. Работа идёт. Поезд идёт. Дорога идёт. Собрание идёт.» — DLI, Lesson 19.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: It rained for three days on end.
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Другим ___ (повезти — to take off (by vehicle)) меньше.
exercises.why: **повезло** is the past tense (neuter) of **повезти** (to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport) — the perfective of **везти**, «set out». past: он повёз · она повезла́ · оно повезло́ · они повезли́. — Wiktionary, «повезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **повезти**: to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport; (impersonal) to be lucky, to have luck, to work out for, to succeed, to be successful [with dative ‘for someone’ and infinitive ‘to do something’].  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: Он ___ (вести — to lead, take along, one way) себя странно.
exercises.why: **ведёт** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **вести** (to lead, to preside over, to chair) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **водить** for many directions. present: я веду́ · ты ведёшь · он ведёт · мы ведём · вы ведёте · они веду́т. — Wiktionary, «вести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **вести**: to lead, to preside over, to chair; to drive; to keep.  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «вести — Страна ведёт войну. — The country is waging a war. · Девочка ведёт дневник. — The girl keeps a diary. · Дорога ведёт в город. — The road leads to the city. · Ложь к добру не ведёт. — No good comes from lying.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «This verb also follows the pattern of "going verbs". Note the following meanings: 1. to lead, to take: Я веду моего сына в школу. Я каждый день вожу его в школу. 2. to drive: Кто ведёт эту машину? Он не умеет водить машину. 3. to conduct: Противник ведёт огонь. 4. to behave oneself: Этот мальчик плохо ведёт себя. Note that in the last two examples (3 and 4) only the actual function verb "вести" can be used. (Never "водить").» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **везло** is the past tense (neuter) of **везти** (to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **возить** for many directions. past: он вёз · она везла́ · оно везло́ · они везли́. — Wiktionary, «везти» (CC BY-SA 4.0). See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «везти — Ей везёт / повезло. — She is lucky/got lucky.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note also the following idiomatic construction: Мне не везёт. — I am not lucky.
